title: Which numbers fill the blanks in twenty five divided by a blank?
description: Six blanks around twenty five. Compare each answer with twenty five to find the divisor, then see that dividing by ten is multiplying by one tenth, and dividing by one tenth is multiplying by ten.
teaching_notes: One idea: dividing by a number and multiplying by its partner give the same result, ten and one tenth being partners. Watch for students who write ten where one tenth belongs.

video_script.why: The child can divide by a decimal on paper but does not see it as multiplying by a partner number.
video_script.substitution: Dividing by ten is multiplying by one tenth, dividing by one tenth is multiplying by ten, and dividing by one hundredth is multiplying by a hundred.
video_script.anchor: Six blanks next to twenty five, three on a division and three on a multiplication
video_script.payoff_line: Twenty five divided by zero point zero one is twenty five times a hundred.

final_answer.spoken: one thousand, zero point one, ten, zero point one, ten and a hundred

maths_rules: 25 / 10 = 25 x 0.1, so the fourth blank is 0.1
25 / 0.10 = 25 x 10, so the fifth blank is 10
25 / 0.01 = 25 x 100, so the sixth blank is 100
video_script.design: Each blank is found by asking how the answer compares with twenty five; the last blank is found by counting how many hundredths fit in one whole.

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about filling blanks.

<bookmark mark='abc'/>In the first three lines, twenty five divided by a blank gives three answers. <bookmark mark='abc2'/>They are zero point zero two five, two hundred and fifty, and two point five.

<bookmark mark='def'/>The last three divide twenty five by ten, then by zero point one zero. <bookmark mark='def2'/>The third divides by zero point zero one. Each one equals twenty five times a blank.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>What number goes in each of the six blanks?

beats.on_screen: the six lines and their blanks stay on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: Compare each answer with 25: a smaller answer needs a big divisor; a bigger answer needs a divisor below 1

marks.same: the number twenty five is placed in the middle of the board
marks.small: an arrow points down to a smaller answer
marks.big: an arrow points up to a bigger answer

narration: <bookmark mark='same'/>We solve this the same way as the example in your book. We compare each answer with twenty five.
<bookmark mark='small'/>A smaller answer means we divided by a big number.
<bookmark mark='big'/>A bigger answer means we divided by a number below one.

beats.on_screen: Given: six lines with blanks, all using 25

marks.given: the six lines are written under each other

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, six lines, and every one has the number twenty five.

beats.on_screen: To find: the number in each blank
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the number that fits in each blank.

beats.on_screen: 25 ÷ ___ = 0.025: the answer is much smaller; the decimal point moves 3 places left; blank = 1000

marks.s1b: the decimal point of 25 moves three places left to give 0.025

narration: <bookmark mark='s1a'/>Step one, twenty five divided by a blank is zero point zero two five.
<bookmark mark='s1b'/>The answer is much smaller. The decimal point has moved three places to the left.
<bookmark mark='s1c'/>Moving it three places divides by one thousand. The blank is one thousand.

beats.on_screen: 25 ÷ ___ = 250: the answer is 10 times bigger; one whole has 10 tenths; blank = 0.1

marks.s2b: one whole is split into ten tenths

narration: <bookmark mark='s2a'/>Step two, twenty five divided by a blank is two hundred and fifty.
<bookmark mark='s2b'/>The answer is ten times bigger than twenty five. One whole has ten tenths in it.
<bookmark mark='s2c'/>Each whole in twenty five gives ten, so the blank is zero point one.

beats.on_screen: 25 ÷ ___ = 2.5: the answer is 10 times smaller; blank = 10

marks.s3b: 25 is shown shrinking ten times to 2.5

narration: <bookmark mark='s3a'/>Step three, twenty five divided by a blank is two point five.
<bookmark mark='s3b'/>The answer is ten times smaller than twenty five.
<bookmark mark='s3c'/>Dividing by ten does that, so the blank is ten.

marks.s4c: ten strips of 0.01 are laid on a whole, and the count continues past the edge of the screen

narration: <bookmark mark='s4a'/>Step four, the lines on the right. Dividing by ten is the same as multiplying by one tenth, so that blank is zero point one.
<bookmark mark='s4b'/>Dividing by zero point one zero is the same as multiplying by ten, so that blank is ten.
<bookmark mark='s4c'/>For the last line, count how many pieces of zero point zero one fit in one whole.

marks.s5b: 25 × 0.1 = 2.5 is written beside it and the two are joined

narration: <bookmark mark='s5a'/>Step five, check one pair. Twenty five divided by ten is two point five.
<bookmark mark='s5b'/>Twenty five times zero point one is also two point five. The two lines agree.

marks.ans: the last blank is filled and boxed
marks.rest: the other five blanks are boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Twenty five divided by zero point zero one is twenty five times a hundred.
<bookmark mark='rest'/>The other blanks, in order, are one thousand, zero point one, ten, zero point one, and ten.
